Website development with AI: costs and scope

Prices, stages and the RESET approach. What has become more accessible and what makes up a finished product’s budget.

01

What landing pages, websites and CRM systems cost

RESET development examples: NIVELLUX website, $600; SHEPIT HOUSE website, $1000; Estate CRM for DELMAR, $2000. These figures refer to specific agreed scopes. A new project is priced according to structure, content, features and integrations.

AI can accelerate parts of the work: prototyping, coding, testing individual solutions and repetitive operations. Savings depend on the product and what must be ready at handover.

One business needs a service page and contact details. Another needs a website for advertising, daily property uploads and enquiry delivery to sales.

NIVELLUX

$600

Company website: services, projects and estimate enquiries.

SHEPIT HOUSE

$1000

Development website with a site plan and instalment calculator.

Specific project costs reported by RESET, in US dollars. These are not universal tariffs.

Projects and development costs
ProjectCostScope
NIVELLUX$600Services, portfolio, estimate requests, Russian and Spanish versions
SHEPIT HOUSE$1000Website with site-plan selection and an instalment calculator
Estate CRM for DELMAR$2000Enquiries, properties, selections and integrations

The SHEPIT HOUSE figure covers website development. Advertising and other work in the wider case study are not included. New project scope and cost are agreed separately.

Even two landing pages can require very different effort. One client brings finished copy, photographs and a clear offer. Another needs product research, positioning, structure, materials and enquiry routing.

Page count is only a rough indicator. A single page with property matching, payment calculations and several integrations may require more work than a small informational website.

02

Using AI to build, building yourself and adding AI to a website

Pricing discussions often mix three tasks.

Building your own site with AI or a builder. The owner pays for tools and invests their time, making decisions about structure, content, services and checks.

Hiring a team that uses AI. The client receives an agreed result; the team chooses the tools. This is the main focus here.

Embedding AI in the product. Natural-language property search, a client assistant or automatic enquiry handling creates additional design, integration and testing work. Depending on the solution, model usage and data processing may carry recurring costs.

A site built with AI may have no AI features for visitors. Clarify that distinction when discussing the budget.

03

Is development with AI cheaper?

With equivalent requirements, AI can reduce effort in particular stages. Savings depend on the task, team experience, source data and verification time.

A controlled GitHub Copilot experiment published in 2023 found that developers with AI access completed a JavaScript HTTP server task 55.8% faster than the control group. It demonstrates acceleration for that task, not a universal reduction in website budgets. GitHub Copilot productivity study.

Consider a hypothetical 100-hour project. If 40 hours of work can be completed twice as quickly and everything else stays the same, the project takes 80 hours: a 20% time saving.

Real estimates also include review, fixes and tool costs. The share of work that can be accelerated varies.

When comparing development with and without AI, compare equivalent features, design, integrations, testing and support. Mentioning AI in a proposal does not explain its price.

04

Where RESET starts

We begin with the business objective: what the company wants after launch and how the product will be used daily.

For a website, we discuss the offer, audience and traffic. Will Google Ads run? Is organic search planned? Are separate pages needed for services, neighbourhoods or property types? Who handles enquiries?

These answers shape the structure before the first screen.

An agency advertising apartments in several areas may need dedicated landing pages and the selected property included in enquiries from the first version. A general destination would leave visitors searching for the advertised offer.

Related / RESET JournalConnecting search queries, advertising and websites

A CRM starts with staff workflows: who receives enquiries, how ownership is assigned, which statuses are used and what management needs to see.

Features and estimates follow that understanding.

05

From business requirements to a working product

RESET follows a sequence: objective, documentation, specification, prototype, implementation and verification.

Preparation scales with the project. A small landing page needs a compact brief; a custom CRM with roles and integrations needs more detail.

  1. 01

    Document the project

    Describe users, actions, data, external services and constraints.

    For property websites, identify listing sources, update responsibility, languages and enquiry destinations. For a CRM, define entities, access and movement between stages.

    Separate essential first-version features from later additions.

    Outcome: a shared framework that the client and team can check for alignment.

  2. 02

    Prepare the specification

    Translate expectations into concrete requirements.

    “Convenient search” needs detail: available parameters, filter combinations, no-results behaviour and shareable selection links.

    For forms, define required fields, recipients, source tracking and error handling.

    Outcome: a basis for estimating and acceptance, with clear implementation and verification criteria.

  3. 03

    Build a prototype

    Show the structure and journeys before full implementation.

    Clients can find an offer, open a property, read terms and enquire; staff can test future CRM workflows.

    Missing information, extra steps and awkward sequences are easier to spot. AI helps produce and change prototypes before all data and services are connected.

    Outcome: agreed interface logic and key actions.

  4. 04

    Develop and connect systems

    Implement the interface and features, then connect data and services.

    A website may need CMS, catalogue, forms, CRM and analytics. Internal systems may need roles, imports, history and automatic actions.

    Agreed decisions make AI tasks more precise: the team knows required behaviour and constraints.

    Outcome: a working version with agreed functionality and integrations.

  5. 05

    Verify journeys and prepare launch

    Test the actions the product exists to support.

    For property enquiries, verify contact and property storage. For database updates, check prices and statuses. For analytics, compare events with actual actions.

    Also check mobile behaviour, key-page speed and content management.

    Agree account handover, maintenance and future changes for the project.

    Outcome: a verified product and a clear post-launch process.

06

Why advertising and SEO should be considered early

Traffic sources shape content and structure.

Search advertising needs to continue the user's intention after the click. Meta visitors may need more explanation after discovering an offer in their feed. Organic search needs pages planned around specific queries.

Requirements discovered after completion can force rework.

Separate campaign pages may be missing, the CMS may lack required fields, or forms may fail to pass the enquiry source.

We therefore clarify audience acquisition and measurement at the outset.

Related / RESET JournalBuilding pages around search demand

See Meta Ads for real estate for lead quality and sales follow-up.

Technical SEO preparation and ongoing promotion have different scopes. Development does not automatically include regular articles, landing-page expansion and all organic acquisition work.

07

How content, design and data affect price

Content can represent a substantial share of the project.

Approved copy, photographs, specifications and translations can be used directly. Missing materials require positioning, writing, image selection and fact-checking.

AI helps draft alternatives. Actual purchase terms, service details, benefits and limitations must come from the business or verified sources.

A ready-made visual foundation and a custom interface also involve different workloads. Unique screens, component states, mobile adaptation and interactions affect estimates.

Property data deserves particular attention. Even existing exports can contain duplicates, inconsistent area names, missing fields or unavailable photographs. Preparation and checks belong in the plan.

Ask what each page contains and where it comes from, alongside how many pages there will be.

08

When building with AI yourself makes sense

Self-building can be reasonable for a limited task when the owner has time to learn and can verify the result.

It can produce a prototype, test service presentation, create a small information page or demonstrate a workflow.

RESET also works with people who started independently and need help finishing. Their work helps explain the concept and requirements.

We assess what works, where data lives, what can be extended and what needs changing.

Handover to specialists is possible, but completion costs require inspection. Finished screens may hide substantial integration, storage and error-handling work.

Even experienced developers need verification. In the 2025 Stack Overflow survey, 66% of respondents to the question on AI frustrations selected solutions that were almost right but needed fixing. This describes respondents' experience, not the error rate of all generated code. Stack Overflow Developer Survey 2025.

09

Why custom CRM needs a separate estimate

Websites typically start with visitor needs. A CRM reflects internal processes and their relationships.

One client may consider several properties, speak with multiple agents and return months later. History, ownership and deduplication need decisions.

Access rights, reports, existing data imports and service connections add requirements.

Before estimating custom development, identify what ready-made software covers and where specific logic is necessary. This establishes a justified scope.

AI may speed up functions, but company rules still need to be described and checked with their users.

10

Costs after launch

Creation and operation should be discussed separately.

Domain, hosting, licences, integration maintenance, content updates and support may remain. Embedded AI can add model usage charges.

Some costs are fixed; others depend on load, users or processing.

Decide what the owner can edit. Requiring a developer for each price or photo update affects ownership costs.

Request recurring charges and future development terms before commissioning.

11

How to reduce the development budget

The most practical saving is a clearly agreed first-version scope.

If an agency needs advertising for one development, start with that journey. Add a large catalogue, accounts and complex automation when demand is established.

Prepared materials, service access, process descriptions and an available decision-maker also help.

Prototypes resolve uncertainty early. Detailed requirements reduce different interpretations. AI accelerates suitable tasks within a clear plan.

Forms, data transfer and key actions still need adequate launch checks because the business relies on them.

12

What RESET needs for an estimate

Describe what you want to create, who needs it and which problem it should solve.

  • Business objective and intended users.
  • Advertising and search plans.
  • Data, services and integrations.
  • Readiness of copy, images and translations.
  • Target timing and first-version priorities.

Existing sites, prototypes, references and self-built versions help define essentials, phases and scope.

RESET examples are NIVELLUX at $600, SHEPIT HOUSE at $1000 and Estate CRM for DELMAR at $2000. Each refers to an agreed scope; a new project is estimated by structure, content, functions and integrations.

AI creates opportunities to save effort. Clear documentation and systematic checking turn those savings into a product that meets agreed needs and supports future work.

13

Before starting

What does an AI-assisted website cost at RESET?

Examples: NIVELLUX $600, SHEPIT HOUSE $1000 and Estate CRM for DELMAR $2000. These are specific scopes. New projects depend on structure, content, functionality and integrations.

Is SEO included?

SEO preparation is specified in the scope. Ongoing promotion, articles and new landing pages are agreed separately.

Can you finish a site I built myself?

Yes. We first inspect its condition and determine the remaining work.

Will I pay for AI after launch?

Using AI only during development does not itself create a subscription for the owner. Platforms and services may charge their own fees. Embedded AI features may need recurring payments.
